question: At what empirically observed reuse horizons, if any, does sending the shared zlib dictionary once reduce total bytes versus persistent zlib without a dictionary?

comparison.baseline: persistent zlib level 9, one stream, LF delimiter per message, Z_SYNC_FLUSH per message, Z_FINISH at horizon
comparison.dictionary_arm: same persistent zlib stream and flush policy with the fixed v0.2 shared dictionary
comparison.accounting: dictionary sent once per seed/stream plus exact compressed stream bytes; no amortization or linear extrapolation
comparison.positive_value_means: dictionary arm transmits fewer total bytes at that horizon

predictions: At the measured horizon of 128 episodes, the dictionary arm remains larger than the no-dictionary stream for all four codecs, consistent with v0.2.
The labeled text, compact JSON, and delimited tuple may cross break-even by 16384 episodes, but stream behavior can make the exact threshold differ from the prior linear extrapolation.
The fixed-width rank arm does not cross break-even within 16384 episodes because the dictionary does not reduce its compressed payload in v0.2.
limits: Model-free byte accounting only; model tokens, inference, latency, and decoder implementation cost are not measured.
One task distribution, schema, dictionary, compressor level, serialization, and point-to-point setup boundary.
Each horizon is an independently finished stream; actual deployment loss recovery, random access, and synchronization are out of scope.
These codec results are controls, not evidence that an LLM can emit or decode any representation.
